restaurant_name: วงศ์สว่างสหคลินิก
text: This is the worst clinic I've ever seen in my life. They severely restrict referrals, most recently limiting them to only 35 patients per day, and only accepting patients on Tuesdays and Thursdays a week. Patients must go in person. Bedridden patients need to provide photos proving their condition. My father went to request a referral letter at 4 AM, only to find out the queue was full and he couldn't get a slot. I learned from other patients that some had been queuing since 9 PM the day before the clinic opened. Referrals are extremely difficult; they constantly refuse referrals, citing that the clinic has specialist doctors. In reality, this is beyond the capabilities of primary care, and the patients are vulnerable and seriously ill, requiring referral to hospitals with the necessary equipment and specialist care. Patients' lives aren't a business; the clinic isn't just about making money. A referral letter means the condition is beyond the clinic's authority and there's a genuine need. I feel sorry for the patients; they were already ill and now they have to suffer through long waits and emotional distress. The clinic's ethics are terrible, the staff are rude, and it's incredibly difficult to contact them. I called until my hand was numb and no one answered. If you have other options, please avoid this clinic. Another thing is that they don't care about any suggestions or criticisms here. People complain to the NHSO every day, but nothing seems to progress. It's a pity for the sick people!

restaurant_name: วงศ์สว่างสหคลินิก
text:
A case study from a patient using the universal healthcare scheme at this clinic:
A family member was refused a referral to a destination hospital by the clinic, despite having a severe heart condition requiring a specialist. The patient had coronary artery stenosis and had already undergone balloon angioplasty at a hospital, and also had other complications such as thyroid cancer. (The destination hospital had been caring for the patient for approximately four years through a referral by the local public health unit, but the patient's healthcare coverage was transferred from the public health unit to this clinic about a year ago.) The clinic claimed to have a competent doctor and therefore did not need to refer the patient to the hospital. However, the reality was that the clinic lacked a cardiology specialist and the treatment was substandard. For example, they refused blood tests, claiming that such tests required an order from the National Health Security Office (NHSO) (which is not the correct procedure). Furthermore, a doctor from the hospital who had been treating the patient for a long time called the clinic to inform them that the patient was in a vulnerable group with complications and deserved continuous care from a specialist. Despite this, the clinic still refused a referral to the destination hospital due to budget limitations imposed by the government, citing insufficient funds for management. These problems should not burden the lives of Thai patients.
Human lives are not mere objects for profit. Clinics that lack substandard public health services and ethical compassion should not be allowed to treat patients, thus creating negative karma for all parties involved. In Buddhism, this could be considered a grave sin, an unwholesome act of dishonesty in the profession and harming patients. These karmic consequences will inevitably fall upon those involved in the act.

They told me to reschedule my appointment with the hospital. They also posted a sign announcing new referral regulations, which I only learned about when I visited the clinic.

Announcement
Referral Times
Tuesday, 8:30 AM - 12:00 PM
(Accepting 35 cases)
Thursday, 8:30 AM - 12:00 PM
(Accepting 35 cases)
Effective February 11, 2025 onwards
Announced on February 7, 2025

Referral Regulations
1. Referrals will be issued only on Tuesdays and Thursdays. 2. Patients must come in person.
3. Request a referral three days before the appointment.
4. Original ID card/birth certificate.
5. Medical history, with one copy.
6. Hospital appointment slip, with one copy.
8:30 AM - 12:00 PM

A conversation with the grandmothers, aunts, and uncles who were affected by the situation, who told me about the situation.

-If you want to be sure of a spot, you have to wait in front of the clinic at 2:00 or 3:00 AM.
- Requesting medical records from the hospital takes a considerable amount of time, typically two weeks or more, to be used in the referral.
- One woman recounted having to reschedule her appointment with the hospital two or three times before a referral was issued.
- Another recounted that her father, who has Alzheimer's, requested medical records. Of course, the hospital takes time to compile them. Everyone understands this, but wouldn't the clinic's request for patients to request them from the hospital each time increase the burden on the hospital and the patient?

Patients are already sick. Don't make them suffer more. Patients will die because of regulations that trample on your patients.

I hope the NHSO will address this issue.

Thank you.
